name: bischoff_no_pda
description: Reference values for the Bischoff et al. 2021 no-PDA group (n = 15; 25.5 wk, 764 g current weight) at ~72 h: Bischoff's measured values where the paper has them, the preterm_25wk set for the rest. Grades as preterm_25wk: A = 24-27 wk infants on day 2-4 (and the Bischoff cohort itself), B = wider band / other day / derived from cohort numbers, C = textbook / extrapolation / derived.
state: Bischoff 2021 no-PDA group: 25.5 wk, 764 g, at 72 h; spontaneous breathing represented as CPAP (mean airway pressure 6, FiO2 0.21, recruited lung), duct closed, PFO open, untransfused, trophic feeds + PN, caffeine, incubator ~36 degC / 80 % RH

variables.label: Heart rate
variables.notes: Bischoff 2021 Table 2, no-PDA group: 155.1 +/- 9.1.

variables.label: Systolic BP
variables.notes: Elsayed Table 4, 25 wk D3 (P5/P25/P50/P75/P95 39/42/45/51/58), UAC, n=29 at 25 wk; bundle with caffeine, delayed clamping, early non-invasive support. Cuff cross-check: van Zadelhoff calculator GA 25+0 PNA 72 h 53.2 (43.2-64.3).

variables.label: Mean arterial pressure
variables.notes: Elsayed 25 wk D3 P5/P25/P50/P75/P95 27/30/34/38/42. Cuff reads only ~1.7 mmHg higher at 25 wk (van Zadelhoff 35.7, P2.3-P97.7 26.4-46.5); <26 wk had routine arterial lines alongside the cuff.

variables.label: Pulse pressure
variables.notes: Derived from the Elsayed medians (28 wk: 25).

variables.label: Central venous pressure
variables.notes: User decision (6.2): Choi 2015 VLBW 3.5 +/- 2.2 (mean +/- 1 SD), steady days 1-7. Revised from 5 (Trevor Inglis 2007, 27 wk, median 4.9, IQR 4.4-6.1), because those infants were mostly ventilated and positive pressure raises CVP; a CPAP infant sits closer to Choi. CPAP impedes systemic venous return (Abdel-Hady 2008).

variables.label: Pulmonary artery pressure, systolic
variables.notes: Derived: RV/systemic systolic pressure ratio 0.60 (user's choice; 28 wk 0.55; Skinner 1992 0.44 healthy / 0.72 HMD) x SBP 45 = 27. Patel 2019: PAAT rises linearly with GA at birth, so relative RV afterload is higher at 25 wk. Ratio grade B, mmHg grade C.

variables.label: Pulmonary artery pressure, mean
variables.notes: Derived from pap_s with the Chemla relation (0.61 x sPAP + 2); extrapolation.

variables.label: Pulmonary artery pressure, diastolic
variables.notes: Constraint, not a measurement: pure L->R flow through a restrictive duct needs PA pressure below aortic pressure through the whole cycle, so PA diastolic < aortic diastolic (~26).

variables.label: LV end-diastolic volume
variables.notes: Groves EF ~65 % kept (no GA effect), scaled to SV 1.10 (user decision): 2.07 x 1.10/1.34.

variables.label: LV end-systolic volume
variables.notes: EDV - SV, scaled as EDV.

variables.label: LV stroke volume
variables.notes: LVO 170 / HR 155 = 1.10; LV VTI 7.8 cm x LVOT area (0.36 cm) / 0.764 kg = 1.04.

variables.label: LV ejection fraction
variables.notes: Groves MRI 69 +/- 5.7 (LLN 58), no GA effect. Homedi 2026 (<29 wk, <=72 h, survivors) echo 59 (55-63); non-survivors (25 wk) 41.

variables.label: RV end-diastolic volume
variables.notes: Derived from RV SV 1.10 at EF ~50 % (as preterm_25wk).

variables.label: RV end-systolic volume
variables.notes: Derived.

variables.label: RV ejection fraction
variables.notes: 3D echo RVEF 52 % (Toyoshima, day 14 controls). FAC is a different index.

variables.label: RV fractional area change
variables.notes: Levy 2015 (23-28 wk, 24-72 h) ~26 +/- 4 %; James 2015 (<29 wk) day 1 31 %, days 5-7 49 % without PDA; Homedi 2026 survivors 45 %. Reference only.

variables.label: TAPSE
variables.notes: Koestenberger 2011 slope 0.039 cm/wk extrapolated to 25 wk. Sehgal 2022 (24.6 wk, day ~20) 0.49; Sehgal 2019 0.45 -> 0.53 after MIST (29.5 wk); Homedi 2026 survivors 0.6 (27 wk), non-survivors 0.3. Reference only.

variables.label: Left ventricular output
variables.notes: Bischoff 2021 Table 2, no-PDA: 169.7 +/- 43.7 (LV VTI 7.8 cm, LVOT 0.36 cm). With the duct closed LVO = SVC + DAo + coronaries.

variables.label: Right ventricular output
variables.notes: Bischoff 2021 Table 2, no-PDA: 170.3 +/- 39.1 (RV VTI 7.8 cm, RVOT 0.36 cm).

variables.label: LVO/RVO ratio
variables.notes: Bischoff 2021 Table 2, no-PDA: median 0.98 [0.93, 1.1]. With the duct closed, RVO - LVO = the net atrial shunt.

variables.label: SVC flow
variables.notes: User decision: the modified method. Bischoff 2021 Table 2, no-PDA: modified 73.4 +/- 29.4; traditional 107.6 [81.8, 147.5].

variables.label: Descending aorta flow
variables.notes: LVO 170 - SVC 73 - coronaries ~12 = ~85, no ductal steal (no diastolic reversal in any no-PDA infant). Split: SMA 22 + coeliac 20 + kidneys 6 + rest ~37.

variables.label: Cerebral blood flow
variables.notes: User decision: kept at the 28 wk value (brain = 33 % of SVC flow). Derivation for 25 wk gives ~24 (17 mL/100 g/min x brain ~100 g = 143 g/kg): Lundstrom 1995 15.9 at birth on room air; CBF rises day 1 -> 3 and with falling Hb (Pryds 1989); more immature brains extract more O2 (Chock 2022).

variables.label: Intestinal (SMA) flow
variables.notes: Trophic feeds + PN. SMA velocities lower at <=26 6/7 wk (Thompson 2013), rising over days 1-5 (Gursoy 2015). A duct <= 2 mm rarely disturbs organ flow (Hsu 2019).

variables.label: Renal blood flow
variables.notes: Follows the GFR decision: 0.30 mL/min/kg at filtration fraction ~8 % and Hct 41 -> ~6.3 (replaces the provisional 8). Doppler totals (Visser) are overestimates.

variables.label: Coeliac (liver + spleen) flow
variables.notes: As at 28 wk: El-Khuffash 2008 coeliac/LVO > 0.10.

variables.label: Ductal shunt flow (L->R)
variables.notes: No PDA (state).

variables.label: Ductal diameter
variables.notes: No PDA: duct closed (state).

variables.label: Foramen ovale shunt (L->R)
variables.notes: Duct closed, so the net atrial shunt = RVO - LVO = LVO (1/(LVO/RVO) - 1): ~3 at 0.98, +13 at 0.93, -15 at 1.10. Atrial communication in 14/15; 6 L->R, 8 bidirectional/R->L (Table 1).

variables.label: Respiratory rate
variables.notes: Extrapolated a little above the 28 wk 62 (no day-3 CPAP data at 25 wk). Welty 2018 (29.6 wk, CPAP 5-8) 67 +/- 20; Dimitriou 72-80 in week 1.

variables.label: Tidal volume
variables.notes: Non-invasive (no mask) convention, as at 28 wk and term. Caffeine assumed.

variables.label: Minute ventilation
variables.notes: RR 65 x Vt 5.0.

variables.label: Inspiratory time fraction (Ti/Ttot)
variables.notes: As at 28 wk.

variables.label: Respiratory system compliance
variables.notes: Absolute value at 0.7 kg: lungs 0.6 /kg in series with chest wall 7 /kg -> 0.55 /kg.

variables.label: Lung compliance (both lungs)
variables.notes: User decision 0.6 (28 wk 0.8): one LISA dose on a less mature lung. Bhutani 0.44 acute RDS; surfactant +29-64 % (Davis 1988); FiO2 0.41 -> 0.27 after MIST (Sehgal 2019). Dassios 2024: mechanics did not differ between 22-24 and 25-27 wk ventilated infants.

variables.label: Chest wall compliance
variables.notes: More compliant at lower GA: Gerhardt 6.4 /kg (32 wk); Stoecklin 2024 3.0 /kg at 36 wk PMA; diaphragm excursion falls with PMA as the chest wall stiffens (Rehan 2001).

variables.label: Respiratory system resistance
variables.notes: Smaller airways: 28 wk 65 at 1 kg, scaled roughly with 1/size.

variables.label: Functional residual capacity
variables.notes: User decision: CPAP 7. da Silva 1994 (28 wk): +~2.6 mL/kg per cmH2O; a stiffer lung recruits less per cmH2O, so CPAP 7 at 25 wk ~ CPAP 6 at 28 wk.

variables.label: Anatomic dead space
variables.notes: Anatomic 2.2 mL/kg (Murthy 2015, 23-27 wk) plus a larger nasopharynx share at small size; alveolar dead space 0.6 mL/kg at 25-27 wk (Dassios 2024).

variables.label: Inspired O2 fraction
variables.notes: Bischoff 2021 Table 1, no-PDA: FiO2 21 % [21, 33], mean airway pressure 6 [6, 7] (80 % HFJV, 20 % CPAP/NIV-NAVA). Represented as spontaneous breathing with a recruited lung (user decision).

variables.label: Apnoea / periodic breathing
variables.notes: Reference only; Apnea model off at baseline. More frequent than at 28 wk; Pre-Vent: events rise from day 3, peak at 3-4 weeks.

variables.label: SpO2 (pre-ductal)
variables.notes: PaO2 44 on the fetal curve (P50 18.5 standard, ~19 at pH 7.37; Hill n 2.7) -> ~91 %.

variables.label: pH
variables.notes: Bischoff 2021 Table 1, no-PDA: 7.37 [7.34, 7.4]. User decision: keep Bischoff's acid-base at 72 h (no PN acidosis, unlike preterm_25wk).

variables.label: pCO2
variables.notes: Bischoff 2021 Table 1, no-PDA: 43 [37, 50].

variables.label: HCO3
variables.notes: Henderson-Hasselbalch from pH 7.37 and pCO2 43.

variables.label: Base excess
variables.notes: Bischoff 2021 Table 1, no-PDA: 0.5 +/- 3.85.

variables.label: PaO2
variables.notes: Oxygenation index 2.84 [2.3, 5.6] = MAP 6 x FiO2 21 / PaO2 -> PaO2 ~44 (median of a ratio, so approximate).

variables.label: Hb-O2 P50 (standard)
variables.notes: De Halleux 2002: <=27 wk week 1 untransfused 18.5 +/- 0.8, HbF 93 %.

variables.label: Mixed venous O2 saturation
variables.notes: Fick: Hb 13.5, SaO2 0.91, systemic flow = LVO 170, VO2 6 -> CaO2 16.6, extraction 3.5 mL/dL -> SvO2 ~72 %.

variables.label: Oxygen consumption
variables.notes: As at 28 wk; no 25 wk day-3 calorimetry. Bauer 2003 4.7 (25-28 wk, day 6, no support); caffeine +26 %.

variables.label: Respiratory quotient
variables.notes: Glucose-rich PN.

variables.label: Core temperature
variables.notes: Sauer 1984: neutral core 36.7-37.3.

variables.label: Incubator air temperature
variables.notes: 0.7 kg, day 3, RH 80 %: warmer than the 28 wk (35 at 70 %).

variables.label: Incubator relative humidity
variables.notes: Most units keep >= 80 % in week 1 below 26-28 wk; skin water loss at 22-26 wk is high and humidity-dependent (Karlsson 2012).

variables.label: Insensible water loss
variables.notes: J Perinatol 2025 (22-28 wk): 47.7 at 70 % vs 28.8 at 90 % RH; ~40 at 80 %. Reference only.

variables.label: Plasma glucose
variables.notes: User decision 7.0 (calm value; 28 wk 6.5). Hyperglycaemia is common: 58 % of EP infants > 8.3 in week 1, more at lower GA (Alsayigh 2026); > 10 common (Fursule 2026); Liu 2026 day 3 7.4 +/- 2.8.

variables.label: Hemoglobin
variables.notes: User decision 13.5. Birth at 25 wk 15.1 (Jopling regression) + delayed clamping ~+1 - early fall in <29 wk - ~15 mL/kg sampled by 72 h (Puia-Dumitrescu 30 mL/kg in week 1 at 25 wk). No day-3 data for <29 wk (virtually all transfused).

variables.label: Hematocrit
variables.notes: Birth 44.5 % (Jopling regression); <29 wk Hct falls 6 % in the first 4 h.

variables.label: Fetal haemoglobin fraction
variables.notes: De Halleux 2002: 92.9 +/- 1.1 % in <=27 wk before transfusion. Reference only.

variables.label: Blood volume
variables.model_readout: sum of blood compartment volumes / weight
variables.notes: Per kg higher with immaturity and delayed clamping; Aladangady 74 delayed vs 63 early (RBC label); plasma markers read higher.

variables.label: GFR
variables.notes: User decision 0.30 mL/min/kg (0.2-0.5) at BSA 0.0789 m2. Above the Vieux exponential extrapolated to 25 wk (4.03 at day 7, ~3.2 on day 3 = 0.21 mL/min/kg, the engine's renal reference) and below Bueva 1994 ~0.5 (27-31 wk). Needs a deliberate override of the default preterm renal rule.

variables.label: Urine output
variables.notes: Diuretic phase (Lorenz 1995, <=1000 g: 25-96 h). Implies water reabsorption ~0.83 at GFR 0.30.

variables.label: Fractional sodium excretion
variables.notes: Higher in the more immature tubule (28 wk: 5 %). Reference only.

variables.label: Plasma creatinine
variables.notes: Miall 1999: peak 221 at 23-26 wk by 48 h, reflecting maternal creatinine and low GFR. Reference only.
